meta.completionPolicy: YOU ARE NOT DONE UNTIL YOU HAVE COMPLETED 100% OF THE BLUEPRINT. DO NOT STOP. YOU MUST REFINE AT REGULAR INTERVALS TO KEEP THE BLUEPRINT FULL. NEVER SPECIFY ANY ESTIMATE OF EFFORT OR COST. NEVER SPECIFY ANY PRIORITY OF ANY KIND.

globalAlerts.warning: BUILD FIRST: Always run `make build` before running scripts. The osm binary must be up-to-date.
TEST AFTER EVERY CHANGE: Run `go test -short -count=1 -timeout=5m ./...` after each significant change to catch regressions early.
ZERO TOLERANCE: Tests must be isolated -- no host state mutation, no external dependencies, no flaky timing-dependent tests.
PLATFORM COMPATIBILITY: All code must work identically on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
JAVASCRIPT SCRIPTS: All app-specific functionality MUST be modeled as JavaScript scripts using the osm runtime.
RULE OF TWO: Every commit must pass two contiguous issue-free subagent reviews before being committed.

NO GIT CLI: The gitops Go package MUST be used for all git operations. Do NOT introduce exec.Command('git', ...) calls. The ONLY exception is gitops.PullRebase which shells out for rebase (go-git limitation).
GO AS REUSABLE MODULES: Go code must be exposed as reusable, modular implementations accessible via osm script. Never hardcode application-specific logic.
INTERNAL API DISCIPLINE: No shims, no variant accumulation. One implementation, update all call sites.
JS BINDING CONTRACT: No binding may block the event loop. All I/O must return Promises via adapter.Loop().Promisify(). context.Background() is forbidden inside bindings — use the ctx from Require.
NO SHIMS: When migrating a legacy binding to async, REMOVE the old synchronous version entirely. Do NOT keep both. Update ALL call sites.

mandatoryDirectives.contextManagement: Tasks are grouped to be manageable units. Do not attempt to solve all tasks in a single turn.

mandatoryDirectives.ruleOfTwo: Before committing any task's code, invoke strict-review-gate with two independent subagents. Only proceed if both reviews pass contiguously.

replanLog.trigger: bt/require.go context.Background() → bridge.ctx change broke TestIntegration_SharedModeTickerShutdown
replanLog.summary: Reverted bt/require.go. The context.Background() in waitAndResolve is intentional lifecycle design — the Promise must resolve after bridge shutdown. Using bridge.ctx cancels the goroutine before the Promise can settle. waitAndResolve doesn't use the ctx parameter at all — it waits on ticker.Done().
